headline: US stocks ended mostly higher as a chip-led rebound followed Thursday’s AI selloff despite a stronger jobs report lifting Fed rate-hike odds
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) rose about 0.3%, the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) gained about 1.1%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) finished slightly lower near 51,286, and the Russell 2000 (IWM) added around 1% as buyers returned to technology shares after Thursday’s AI-driven wipeout.
- Chip names led the rebound, with Nvidia (NVDA) climbing about 3%, AMD (AMD) rising about 11%, Micron Technology (MU) advancing about 5%, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index up roughly 4%–6%.
- The October jobs report showed nonfarm payrolls up 165,000 versus roughly 65,000 expected, the unemployment rate dipping to 4.1%, and average hourly earnings rising 0.4% to $38.00, pushing December Fed rate-hike odds to about 78% and aligning with San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly’s guidance for higher rates.
- Airbnb (ABNB) jumped more than 10% after CEO Brian Chesky highlighted the company’s fastest revenue growth in three years, raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to the high teens, lifted its adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 36%, and authorized an additional $12 billion in share buybacks.
- DraftKings (DKNG) sank over 20% after posting a larger-than-expected adjusted EBITDA loss and issuing fiscal 2026 revenue guidance below consensus.
- Atlassian (TEAM) slid about 16% after beating first-quarter estimates but guiding to slower cloud and subscription ARR growth.
- Monster Beverage (MNST) declined after reporting a third-quarter gross margin miss.
- Tesla (TSLA) said it plans to wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 at its Giga Texas plant as sales run at roughly 10% of planned capacity, ultimately ending production to refocus on the Cybercab robotaxi program.
- Humana (HUM) gained after boosting its forecast.
- Supplemental commentary noted that no major after-hours earnings reactions exceeded 2% in notable names, with traders turning attention to next week’s inflation data, additional Federal Reserve speakers, and another wave of corporate earnings slated for the week of November 10.
